Issued at 300 PM CDT Thu Oct 8 2026

REST OF TODAY INTO TONIGHT:

Mild temperatures top out in the upper 50s to mid 60s this
afternoon alongside westerly winds with occasional gusts to
15-20 mph through late this afternoon. While there is some weak
shortwave energy traversing the region in northwest flow aloft,
this will mainly result in persisting mix of clouds and clearing
through the rest of today and evening as dry air in the lower 
portions of the atmosphere keeps precipitation from reaching the
ground. The exception would be some patchy sprinkles at best 
(less than 15% chance) near the Brainerd Lakes and along the 
International Border late this afternoon and evening.

Temperatures cool off quickly tonight with calm to light winds
and some lingering cloud cover. Not an ideal radiational cooling
set up for areas where clouds linger. Low temperatures drop into
the low 30s to around 40 degrees, with the areas of best
potential for at or below freezing temperatures in the Iron
Range/interior Arrowhead to the International Border and in
north-central Wisconsin IF breaks in clouds can occur for a 
period of time tonight.

FRIDAY INTO SUNDAY:

Surface high pressure departing to the east will lead to
southerly/southeasterly winds developing on Friday. Temperatures
will be on the increase, reaching the low 60s to around 70F, and
some 50s in the Arrowhead due to onshore flow. Winds should be
on the increase throughout Friday, with PM gusts to 15-25 mph,
steadily increasing overnight. No precipitation is expected.

For Saturday, the Northland will be wedged between an anomalous
upper-level ridge axis centered just to our east and troughing
over the Pacific Northwest. At the surface, a low pressure
system in the Dakotas will have a very tight pressure gradient
out ahead of it, pumping unusually warm and breezy conditions
into the Northland relative to this time of year. Given strong,
southerly warm air advection ahead of the low pressure, high
temperatures are forecast to soar into the upper 70s to mid 80s,
being warmest in the I-35 corridor to northwest Wisconsin. Wind
gusts of 25-35 mph are also expected, as well as minimum
relative humidity dipping to the low to upper 30s (%) in the
warmest areas and upper 30s to 40s (%) elsewhere. This
combination of fairly low relative humidity combined with very
warm and breezy conditions may lead to near-critical fire 
weather conditions on Saturday. We stay in the warm sector of
the low pressure system on Saturday night with breezy warm,
southerly winds continuing. As a result, low temperatures for
many areas shouldn't cool off much below the upper 50s to mid
60s except in far north-central Minnesota. Several locations
could approach record daily high temperatures for Saturday and
record warm low temperatures for Saturday night (see the
"Climate" section below).

On Sunday, the surface cold front associated with the low
pressure system will gradually be moving from northwest to
southeast across the area. Given the current forecast timing of
the front, the I-35 corridor into northwest Wisconsin should
still see high temperatures top out around 80F to the low 80s.
Most of northeast Minnesota should see highs in the 70s, with
some 60s in far north-central Minnesota where the front will
move through quicker. Given later cold front timing in the I-35
corridor to northwest Wisconsin, the warm temperatures, fairly
low min RH, and southerly wind gusts of 20-30 mph late Sunday
morning and afternoon could lead to elevated fire weather
conditions. 

LATE SUNDAY INTO EARLY NEXT WEEK:

Upper-level support/troughing is relatively weak and situated
behind the cold front on Sunday. Far north-central Minnesota
could see light rain chances arrive as early as late Sunday
afternoon or evening, with rain chances then moving across areas
mainly north of US HWY 2 (20-50% chance) Sunday evening and
night. Farther south may not see any precipitation through
Sunday night as drier air appears to linger in the lower levels
of the atmosphere. Areas that do see rain likely see less than 
0.10". 

A second trough aloft moves through the area Monday into Monday
night as a secondary surface low moves across Wisconsin into 
the central Great Lakes. A little bit better scattered, light
rain chances are possible with this second trough across much of
the Northland (40-70%, highest in north-central MN into the
Arrowhead). Regardless, additional accumulations range from
little to nothing south of US HWY 2 to 0.10-0.20" in north-
central Minnesota into the Arrowhead. Total amounts for late
Sunday through Monday night will generally top out around 0.25"
in northern areas, with decreasing amounts with southward
extent to almost no accumulating rainfall south of US HWY 2.

Much cooler, more seasonal October temperatures return Monday
and Tuesday. Lows Monday night are forecast to dip into the low
30s north to low 40s south and low to upper 30s Tuesday night.
